AL.name: Anniston City
AL.quote: the Board permits reasonable corporal punishment of students in Anniston City schools. If such punishment is required, it shall be administered with care, tact, and caution by the principal, assistant principal, or, when appropriate, by their designee. In all cases, however, corporal punishment shall be administered in the presence of the principal or assistant principal. In all cases, corporal punishment shall be administered only by certified personnel.

AL.name: Butler County Schools
AL.quote: The Board shall allow reasonable corporal punishment only after other means of discipline have failed to produce desirable results. If corporal punishment is required, it shall be administered only by a certified employee in the presence of a school administrator who has been informed beforehand of the reasons for the punishment. At no time shall corporal punishment be administered in the presence of another student. Parents who object to corporal punishment as a method of discipline shall advise the school administrator in writing of the objection; however, the school administrator has the authority to determine appropriate discipline
AL.policy_code: 2026-2027 Code of Conduct, section "Corporal Punishment" (p. 14, under Formal Disciplinary Actions and Procedures)
AL.notes: Opt-out only, and non-binding: parents who object must advise the administrator in writing, but the text says the administrator retains authority to determine discipline, and the signature page reads "I DO___ or DO NOT ___ prefer that corporal punishment (paddling) be used ... However, I acknowledge the right of the school system's authority to use any and all disciplinary measures ... including paddling." Administered by a certified employee with a Board-issued paddle, no more than three licks, in the presence of a school administrator (or principal's designee), after an attempted phone call to the parent, recorded in PowerSchool, with a written explanation and witness name given to parents afterward. No disability exemption is stated. Document is the district's "2026-2027 Code of Conduct" PDF linked from https://www.butlerco.k12.al.us/for-parents/bcss-handbook-policies (BCSS Handbook & Policies page), which also lists "Board Policy/Student Handbook & Code of Conduct Revisions" dated July 17, 2025 and October 16, 2025. The Code of Conduct cites Alabama Code 16-28A-1 and Ingraham v. Wright. Corporal punishment is listed as a first-offense option for Class II (grades 6-12) and Class III offenses. No separate board policy manual (AASB-style) was found on the district site; the Code of Conduct is board-adopted and is the operative text.

AL.quote: In accordance with Alabama law, the Board of Education permits the use of corporal punishment. AL.name: DeKalb County Board of Education (DeKalb County Schools)
AL.quote: 6.14.1 Corporal Punishment - Corporal punishment shall always be administered with a consideration for the age and physical maturity of the student. Corporal punishment must always be a deliberate, well thought out action on the part of school administrators and should be administered appropriately to effectively alter student behaviors that are unacceptable in a school environment. Should corporal punishment be needed, it must be administered according to the following: a. A student must be notified of the offense for which he/she is to receive corporal punishment and the student must be given an opportunity to explain his/her actions. b. The punishment must be administered by a school administrator and witnessed by a certified school employee. c. The punishment must be administered out of view of any other students. d. The punishment shall consist of a moderate use of physical force or physical contact by an administrator as may be necessary to maintain discipline or to enforce school rules. e. A written record of the punishment shall be made, in which the violated offense resulting in the punishment is listed along with the administered punishment, the name of the witness(es), and the name of the administrator giving the discipline. The administrator shall maintain a copy of the record and a copy shall be given to the student's parent/guardian.
AL.notes: No parental consent or opt-out; the 2026-2027 Student Handbook and Code of Conduct sec. 5.3.3 states verbatim: 'State law does not forbid corporal punishment. The DeKalb County Board of Education does not recognize a "no paddle" list. Schools must follow IEP/504 plan or make provisions for medical reasons.' Administered by a school administrator, witnessed by a certified employee, out of view of other students, written record with copy to parent. Policy manual is 'Policies and Procedures Handbook', 228 pages, cover reads 'Effective 8/1/2026' (page footers carry 'DRAFT 5/21/15' watermark). Linked from https://www.dekalbk12.org/handbooks. GA.name: Bacon County Schools

Cherokee County School District (GA) does NOT use Simbli; it publishes its own Online Policy Manual as HTML pages at https://www.cherokeek12.net/board-of-education/online-policy-manual (fetched 200, 83,297 bytes, text/html). Section J (Students) lists 27 policies (JAA, JBC, JBC(1), JBC(2), JBC(4), JBCC, JBD, JCAB, JCAC, JCAC(2), JCDAA, JCEB, JD, JDD, JG, JGC, JGCC, JGF, JGF(2), JGI, JHC, JHCB, JHCC, JK, JQK, JR, JS) -- there is no JDA or any policy titled Corporal Punishment, and the whole manual index page contains zero occurrences of the string 'corporal'. Policy JD - Student Discipline (https://www.cherokeek12.net/j-students/jd-student-discipline, 200, 57,597 bytes, text/html; ADOPTED August 2, 2001, REVISED July 16, 2020) says only: 'The Cherokee County Board of Education each year will approve student conduct and discipline procedures in the “Student Code of Conduct.” That Policy, as approved on a yearly basis, is incorporated herein by reference.' That incorporated Code of Conduct SY2026-27 (https://resources.finalsite.net/images/v1785441549/cherokeek12net/wbynmydgcfgtjdnlmus8/CodeofConductSY2026-27.pdf; fetch_document: 7,612,179 bytes, application/pdf, 99 pages, 315,344 chars extracted) returned ZERO hits for 'corporal punishment', 'paddl' and 'spank'. The SY2026-27 Student Parent Handbook (https://resources.finalsite.net/images/v1783513870/cherokeek12net/c1batzough6fn1wncj9n/StudentParentHandbookSY2026-27.pdf; 2,543,337 bytes, application/pdf, 43 pages, 179,406 chars) also returned zero hits. resolve_handbook on cherokeek12.net found no board_policy_systems. The district is silent in every primary document I could open; silence is not a prohibition, so this is filed unknown rather than 'bans' as the legacy map claimed. A reviewer wanting to close this would need a records request or an administrative regulation not published online.

(3) Opened Board Policy JCD Student Conduct (adopted 12/31/1995, revised 07/31/2002) — no corporal-punishment language; the O.C.G.A. 20-2-730/731/732 citations appear only in the non-binding "Policy Reference Disclaimer" table, which the page itself says is "not intended to be part of the policy itself". (4) Opened Board Policy JCDA Student Code of Conduct (adopted 06/30/2000, revised 07/16/2015) — no corporal-punishment language. (5) Scripted a pass over all thirteen lettered sections (A-M) of the manual looking for any policy title matching corporal/paddl/spank — no hit. (6) Fetched the district's current 2026-27 Student Code of Conduct PDF, https://resources.finalsite.net/images/v1784223054/forsythk12gaus/gxs5km2nsgo4cabqy4ft/26-27CodeofConduct.pdf (resolved from https://www.forsyth.k12.ga.us/fs/resource-manager/view/d7b28113-3b63-4c12-bf88-f60711910e18): 681078 bytes, application/pdf, 24 pages, 75405 characters of text, sha256 ede367a4a5f80634de3103be13b68dd7ebb963b6615358356682c6e9a4b123ee — ZERO occurrences of "corporal", "paddl" or "spank". GA.quote: The Peach County Board Of Education permits corporal punishment pursuant to the following requirements:
GA.notes: Board policy on Simbli, read 2026-09-25 by policy code in a sweep of Simbli sites; the district name is from the site's index page. Identity is name and state matched against the federal LEA directory.
quotes: The Peach County Board Of Education permits corporal punishment pursuant to the following requirements:
The corporal punishment shall not be excessive or unduly severe.
Corporal punishment shall never be used as a first line of punishment for misbehavior unless the pupil was informed beforehand that specific misbehavior could occasion its use;
provided, however, that corporal punishment may be used as a first line of punishment for those acts of misconduct which are so antisocial or disruptive in nature as to shock the conscience.

The principal or teacher who administered corporal punishment must provide the child’s parent, upon request, a written explanation of the reasons for the punishment and the name of the principal or assistant principal, who was present;
provided, however, that such an explanation shall not be used as evidence in any subsequent civil action brought as a result of the corporal punishment.

Corporal punishment shall not he administered to a child whose parents or legal guardian has upon the day of enrollment of the pupil filed with the principal of the school a statement from a medical doctor licensed in Georgia stating that it is detrimental to the child’s mental or emotional stability.

MS.name: Calhoun County Schools
MS.quote: Corporal Punishment Reasonable corporal punishment may be administered as a disciplinary measure to preserve an effective learning environment. The superintendent shall enforce rules governing corporal punishment, including the following: 1. Corporal punishment must be reasonable, moderate, and not administered maliciously or for revenge. The student's size, age, and condition must be considered. 2. The principal or a teacher may administer corporal punishment. 3. It must be administered in the presence of another certified staff member and outside the view of other students. 4. Suspensions of up to three days will be used as an alternative to corporal punishment. 5. Parents must notify the school in writing each school year if they refuse corporal punishment. Policy Reference: CCSD Board Policy JDB; Miss. Code Ann. § 37-11-57.

Because the row's name cannot be resolved to one district, and the two districts' policies are NOT the same, I am filing 'unknown' rather than guessing. What I verified, for whoever splits this row: (1) COFFEEVILLE SCHOOL DISTRICT = consent_required. Its Employee Handbook 2024-2025 (https://content.myconnectsuite.com/api/documents/001cf320f7154338a85e5a07e2b90dd2, linked from https://mscoffeevillesd.schoolinsites.com; fetch_document: 1241008 bytes, application/pdf, 65 pages; passage on PDF page 15) states verbatim: 'Reasonable corporal punishment of a student is permitted only with parent/guardian consent.' followed by paddle-size and witness rules. Its board policy manual is at coffeeville.msbapolicy.org -> Simbli S=36031813 (not retrievable - Imperva). (2) WATER VALLEY SCHOOL DISTRICT = not determined. Its 2024-2025 district Parent/Student Handbook (https://core-docs.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/documents/asset/uploaded_file/2769/WVSD/4620788/2024-_2025_WVSD_Handbook.pdf; fetch_document: 2788134 bytes, application/pdf, 112 pages) contains NO occurrence of 'corporal', 'paddl' or 'spank' anywhere. OK.name: Ada
OK.quote: CORPORAL PUNISHMENT It is the policy of the Pontotoc Technology Center Board of Education to administer corporal punishment only as a last resort after other reasonable corrective measures have been used without success.
quotes: CORPORAL PUNISHMENT It is the policy of the Pontotoc Technology Center Board of Education to administer corporal punishment only as a last resort after other reasonable corrective measures have been used without success.
However, under no circumstances shall any child in DHS custody or any student on an individualized educational program (IEP) be administered corporal punishment.
At the beginning of the school year, parents and legal guardians will be provided the opportunity to request the non administration of corporal punishment to their child.
If a request for the non administration of corporal punishment has not been signed, the administration shall notify a parent or legal guardian that corporal punishment is being planned.
At that time, the parent or legal guardian may request that corporal punishment not be administered.

The principal shall notify the parent(s)/guardian(s) any time corporal punishment is used.

A disciplinary record shall be maintained and shall contain the name of the student, the type of misconduct, the type of corporal punishment administered, the name of the person administering the punishment, the name of the witness present, and the date and time of punishment.

phone_policy.policy_code: Student Code of Conduct 2026-2027, General Conduct Violations, 'Possession of Personal Communication Devices' (p. 8)
phone_policy.notes: Listed under 'Students shall not:'. Whole-school-day prohibition with district-mandated storage (turned off in backpack or campus storage). Consequences: 1st offense device confiscated 5 school days, 2nd 10 days, 3rd until end of year, subsequent DAEP. Exceptions only for IEP/504, physician directive, or health/safety requirement. Does not name HB 1481 by number; the exception list mirrors the 2025 Texas law's exceptions.

TX.quote: The administrators of a school are authorized to administer reasonable corporal punishment to a student if it is judged necessary for enforcing school regulations.

contact.public_comment: Board meeting notices are posted at each campus entry door at least 72 hours before the meeting; all meetings are open to the public (no sign-up procedure published).

TX.notes: Gateway Charter Academy 'Student Code of Conduct' (published on the school's own site as 'Student/Parent Handbook'), page 23 of 93; the guidelines continue onto p.24. 597,056 bytes, application/pdf (fetch_document). The PDF carries no adoption date in its text; the Edlio file path dates the upload 2022-03-02 and it is the copy the school currently links from https://www.gatewaycharter.org/apps/pages/index.jsp?uREC_ID=198989&type=d&pREC_ID=429386. Open-enrollment charter in Dallas, not a TASB Policy Online subscriber; no board policy manual is published online. No parental opt-out or opt-in provision appears anywhere in the corporal punishment passage, and corporal punishment is listed as a Group III consequence (p.29).

phone_policy.quote: In accordance with state law, the district prohibits the use of a personal communication device (such as cell phones, tablets, and smartwatches) while on school property during the school day. [...] House Bill 1481, enacted in Texas, prohibits students from using "personal communication devices" during school hours on school property. [...] Designated storage areas will include student backpacks, provided the device(s) are powered off. Use of personal communication devices in restrooms and locker rooms is strictly prohibited.
phone_policy.policy_code: Student Handbook 2026-27, 'Possession and Use of Personal Communications Devices, Including Cell Phones and Other Electronic Devices' (p. 67-68); Student Code of Conduct 2026-27 p. 9; policy FNCE(LOCAL)
phone_policy.notes: Cites Texas HB 1481 by name. 'Administration may grant permission during lunch periods or in emergency situations outside of the classroom.' Four-step consequence ladder ending in daily office lock-up of the device for the rest of the year. Code of Conduct: 'Use a personal communication device, including a cell phone, or other electronic device on school property during the school day and shall store the device in accordance with the method of storage established by the district.'

ai_policy.quote: Utilize artificial intelligence in a way that would constitute academic dishonesty or as a means of engaging in any other prohibited conduct.
ai_policy.policy_code: Student Code of Conduct 2026-27, 'General Conduct Violations'
ai_policy.notes: Also listed among grading-policy items: 'unauthorized use of artificial intelligence, plagiarism'. No stand-alone AI policy in the handbook (searched 'artificial intelligence', 'AI', 'ChatGPT', 'generative').

phone_policy.quote: Use a personal communication device, including a cell phone, or other electronic device on school property during the school day
phone_policy.policy_code: Student Code of Conduct 2026-2027, General Conduct Violations, 'Possession of Telecommunications or Other Electronic Devices' (p. 8)
phone_policy.notes: Listed under 'Students shall not:'. Exceptions only for IEP/504, physician directive, or health/safety requirement. The 2026-2027 MPHS Student Handbook (p. 56) states: 'In accordance with state law, the district prohibits the use of a personal communication device (such as cell phones, tablets, and smartwatches) while on school property during the school day.' and refers to FNCE(LOCAL). HB 1481 is not named by number.

ai_policy.quote: Unauthorized use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools to generate or substantially complete assignments, projects, or assessments is considered academic dishonesty and may result in academic and/or disciplinary consequences consistent with district policy and the Student Code of Conduct.
ai_policy.policy_code: Mount Pleasant Junior High School Student Handbook 2026-2027, 'Grading Policies' (p. 26)
ai_policy.notes: The district Code of Conduct and the MPHS handbook are silent on AI (searched 'artificial intelligence', 'AI', 'A.I.', 'ChatGPT', 'generative'); the Code's academic dishonesty item lists cheating, plagiarism and unauthorized communication only. The junior high handbook is the only MPISD document found that addresses AI, and only as academic dishonesty.

start_times.notes: MPJH runs staggered grade schedules: 7th grade 8:01-3:53, 8th grade 8:05-3:57. MPHS regular schedule (handbook Section V, p. 94) 1st period 8:05, 8th period ends 3:57.

WA.name: Northwest Educational Service District 189
WA.notes: FEDERAL FILING ANOMALY, not an unread policy. This state prohibits corporal punishment in public schools by statute (see data/states), yet the district's 2023-24 CRDC filing reports students receiving it. The project's analysis of these filings (facts/claims/crdc-ban-state-reports-2023-24.md) finds the pattern consistent with restraint or seclusion miscoded as corporal punishment. No district policy permitting the practice can exist lawfully here; the open question is the filing, which belongs to the district and to OCR. Closed 2026-09-24; reopen if the district or OCR corrects the filing.

WY.name: Sublette County School District #1
WY.quote: Corporal punishment does not include the necessary and reasonable use of physical force to defend against physical force or to otherwise prevent a student from injuring himself or others.
quotes: Corporal punishment does not include the necessary and reasonable use of physical force to defend against physical force or to otherwise prevent a student from injuring himself or others.
Corporal punishment also does not apply to the use of reasonable physical force necessary to maintain control and order or to remove a disruptive student from the class or school setting.
The use of corporal punishment in any form is strictly prohibited in the public schools.
No student will be subject to the infliction of corporal punishment by any teacher, other student, administrator, or other school personnel.
No teacher, administrator, student, or other person will subject the student to corporal punishment or condone the use of corporal punishment by any person under his/her supervision or control.
Permission to administer corporal punishment will not be sought or accepted from any parent, guardian or school official.
